_provenance: product-strategist output, persisted VERBATIM as returned on 2026-08-09. The showrunner did not rewrite, rename, trim or summarise any field. Note for the retro: the Phase 4 agents were given Write this run so they persist their own output, and the same argument applies to the discovery room, which still routes through showrunner transcription.

opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: The buy door itself. On 2026-08-09 the ticketing system at tickets.wpyr.com returned an unavailable message pointing customers to the 1-800 line and info@wpyr.com, while the same page rendered an order-processing thank you and a warning not to close the window (c19). This is a point-in-time observation and could be transient, and it must always be said that way. AI is the wrong tool for uptime. What is real here is monitoring plus a deterministic fallback capture form, so a guest who arrives at a closed door leaves a structured, priced, contactable intent instead of a bounce. Evidence strength, three same-day independent observations, so the sighting is solid, the standing condition is unknown.

The reservation office is published as Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM Alaska Time on two independent product pages, so it is standing policy rather than a typo (c10). Cruise arrivals do not respect that window, five ships were listed arriving in Skagway on Sunday August 9, 2026 (c20, third-party schedule aggregator, medium confidence). AI can hold the 128 hours a week the office is shut, answering from their own published material and capturing anything it can't finish. Evidence strength, high on the hours, medium on the arrival pattern.

Cancelling or altering a booking requires a phone call, with no online path published (c11). The refund clock is 24 hours before departure with a $10.00 penalty per person, and inside 24 hours the guest forfeits all rights to a refund (c12). The weekday-only constraint is carried from the product pages (c10), never from the cancellation page, which states no hours. The honest read is that most of this is deterministic software rather than AI, rules can apply a 24 hour clock and a fixed penalty perfectly and can be tested exhaustively. AI's genuine role is upstream, understanding an unstructured request that arrives by email or form at 9pm Saturday and turning it into a structured, timestamped work item. Evidence strength, high, all three claims are the company's own published policy.

The Reservation Agent role explicitly includes answering questions via phone, email and in person regarding White Pass products (c30), which is the same answer given three times through three doors. The contact page offers phone, email, fax and a contact form, with no live chat widget present (c18). AI can absorb the repeat tail, cited to their own pages, and leave the agent the calls that need a person. Evidence strength, high, it is in their own job posting and on their own contact page.

The company states it is actively seeking candidates who can speak other languages fluently, in particular Spanish and Japanese (c31). Language coverage is the one capability that is genuinely hard to hire for in Skagway and genuinely cheap for a model. Machine translation with a human review path on anything that touches money is the safe shape. Evidence strength, high, it is their own recruiting language, and it tells you the demand exists without our having to guess at it.

The Summit excursion is sold through the Princess, Holland America Line, Carnival and Norwegian shore excursion departments with dockside boarding, alongside the direct phone channel (c13). Klondike Holdings includes Carnival PLC as a minority partner (c5), so the channel and part of the ownership sit in the same place. The material AI opportunity is reconciliation and message handling across desks rather than anything guest-facing. Evidence strength, high on the fact of the channel, and NO channel split is published anywhere, so nothing may be sized off it.

Several Skagway operators appear to sell packages built around the railway's own train and price them above the direct fare (c50). That claim was NOT re-verified this pass and any specific price from it must be re-checked before it ships. The general pattern is corroborated by the railway's own product appearing on a cruise line shore excursion page (c13). If it holds, the AI-adjacent opportunity is channel and content consistency, making sure every reseller shows the correct season, exception dates and boarding instruction. Evidence strength, low to medium, flagged.

Published 2026 fares are flat and public, Summit at $155 adult and $77.50 child, Bennett at $289 and $144.50, Steam Summit Loop at $249 and $180, and the rest (c15). The Points Guy, having checked both channels, reports the direct online fare at $155 adult against Norwegian's listed $229 adult, and notes the popular train rides usually sell out in advance (c14). Amtrak's ARROW revenue management system achieved an average additional revenue of 3 to 5 percent, the only quantified figure in that peer-reviewed survey (c43). This is the largest theoretical upside in the whole map and it is also the least buildable today, because no passenger count, no trains-per-day and no channel split are published, so there is no demand signal to model. Evidence strength, high on the fares, high on the Amtrak precedent, and zero on their own demand data.

opportunity_map.area: Train operations scheduling against ship arrivals
opportunity_map.what_ai_could_change: Almost 2,000 train starts run through the summer season (c7), against a published Summit season of April 30 to October 7, 2026 with stated no-service dates of May 2 to 4, September 26 to 27, and October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), and a Bennett season of May 26 to September 12, 2026 (c17). Optimisation against ship arrivals is a classic scheduling problem and it is mostly a solver problem, not an AI one. Evidence strength, medium, the shape is published but no trains-per-day figure exists to build against.

Reservation Agents are pulled onto the platform to assist the Passenger Department with train loading, passenger transfers and crossing-guard duties (c30). That is the labour collision worth naming, the same person is both the contact centre and the loading crew, so every avoidable call lands during the moment they are least able to take it. AI does not load a train. It can make sure the phone is quieter while the train is loading. Evidence strength, high, their own job description.

Six 30-class engines are currently in Skagway, with the seventh and eighth to be delivered in 2026 (c36). Note the page says currently in Skagway, not in service. Predictive maintenance is a real category on rail, and there is no cited maintenance pain here, no telemetry, and no evidence of a data source. Parked deliberately. Evidence strength, thin, map only.

The railroad employs 180 people, most of them based in Skagway (c3), across depot offices in Skagway, Carcross YT and Whitehorse YT (c1), and lists a May 1 to September 30, 2026 recruiting season (c35, recruiting copy). On 2026-08-09 Reservation Agent was listed among open 2026 positions in Carcross and Whitehorse, and was not listed for Skagway (c32, absence from a list, not an affirmative closed marking). Fortune reported on June 2, 2026 that Chipotle's time from application to first day dropped from 12 days to four after a conversational hiring assistant, with about 30 percent of scheduling work now happening after hours (c46, Fortune's own voice, and Chipotle is enormous so the direction transfers and the magnitude does not). This is the best MEASURED evidence in the file and the weakest evidence of a pain at this company, because no time-to-hire, applicant volume or turnover figure is published and no year-round versus seasonal headcount split exists. Evidence strength, strong on the industry precedent, inferred on the local pain.

About 40 workers, including tour guides, announcers and workers who greet visitors as they leave their cruise ships, voted to join SMART-TD's local chapter on April 8, and the company said its employees have the right to organize and it looks forward to working with its onboard staff in this new capacity (c33). This is a constraint on the map, not an opportunity. Anything that touches the terms, scheduling or monitoring of the named group is a negotiation, not a deployment. Worth noting that Reservation Agents are not among the roles named in the unit. Evidence strength, high, and treated as a guardrail.

A Controller is published on the company directory. Shoretime, the cloud platform built specifically to run cruise shore-excursion operations end to end and partnered with Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings since February 2024, sells exactly this work, unifying the bid portal with sales, operations and settlement, eliminating duplication of tasks, integrating email and system messages into a single inbox and automating supplier invoicing, and it makes no artificial-intelligence claim anywhere on its site (c41). The people closest to this workflow, with every commercial incentive to say AI, are not saying it. The honest conclusion is that this area is a buy decision, not an AI build. Evidence strength, high, and it points away from us.

A Manager of Marketing and Product Development is published. A navigation link labelled FAQ points to the travel blog, and that page carries no frequently-asked-questions content (c34). That last item is evidence only and low-value evidence at that, it may never be a headline, an opening sentence or a framed finding, and it is not one here. Content generation is the commodity end of AI and it is not where this business hurts. Evidence strength, low, map only.

Season dates, service exception dates and the cancellation policy live on separate pages, and the weekday hours live on product pages rather than on the cancellation page (c10, c11, c12, c16, c17). A single governed source of truth for policy text, feeding the site, the answer layer and any partner desk, is a real and unglamorous win. Evidence strength, medium, inferred from where the facts actually sit.

A Gift Shop Manager is published, and Carnival's release describes the transaction as covering port, railroad and retail operations in Alaska (c6). No retail pain is cited anywhere. Parked. Evidence strength, none beyond existence.

ZERO verbatim customer reviews were obtainable, TripAdvisor, Yelp, Cruise Critic and KHNS all returned HTTP 403 to every attempt, so this study may not characterise what customers say. That is a limit on US, not a finding about them. The genuine opportunity is first-party, a post-ride feedback capture that turns unstructured comments into themes the company owns rather than rents from a platform. Evidence strength, none on their current state, which is precisely the point.

No CIO, IT director, IT manager or technology lead appears anywhere on the published directory, and no COO, CEO, GM or Director of Operations title is published either. This is an unverified inference about capability and must never be stated as a fact about the company, it may only be described as what their own published directory does and does not list. Its only legitimate use is to shape delivery, favouring managed and low-maintenance builds over anything that assumes an in-house engineer. Evidence strength, it is an absence, treated as one.

Only 12 percent of tour, activity and attraction operators actively use AI in their operations, with most still experimenting or not using it at all, from Arival's survey of more than 7,000 operators published October 22, 2024 (c42). Alaska Railroad runs a customer-facing chatbot branded Ask Denali, verified on one page (c40). No AI feature was found on any Skagway operator site fetched, and that is a floor rather than a proof of absence, because chat widgets are usually JavaScript-injected and a markdown fetch will not always see them (c53, not re-verified). FareHarbor markets an AI guest-communication product with no named customer, no pricing and no measured outcome, and that page was not re-verified, so it is vendor marketing and not evidence of anything working (c49). Evidence strength, high on Arival, medium on Ask Denali, flagged on the rest.

outcome: By the opening of the 2027 season, resolve the majority of guest contacts that arrive outside the published Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM reservation window without a return phone call, and cut the share of in-window agent time spent on repeat questions, measured on four falsifiable counters that do not exist today. One, the number of guest contacts arriving outside the office window per week and the share closed without an agent touching them. Two, median time from a contact arriving outside the window to a resolution the guest can act on, against a baseline that is currently the next business morning at best. Three, the share of change and cancellation requests that reach the office with a timestamp earlier than the 24 hour refund cutoff, against a baseline of zero because there is no path to record one today. Four, agent-handled repeat-question volume during the hours a train is loading. Note honestly that counters one and four have no published baseline, no passenger count, no trains-per-day figure and no channel split exist, so the first four weeks of any build are a measurement exercise before they are a savings claim.

opportunities.job: When my plans change after Friday afternoon, I want to change or cancel my train booking and know exactly where I stand on my money, so I don't lose the fare or the seat.
opportunities.current_workaround: Phone the 1-800 line and hope it is a weekday inside an eight hour window, or wait until Monday and discover the 24 hour clock already ran out, or eat the loss and no-show.
opportunities.notes: The single highest-scoring job because the guest's money is on a 24 hour clock while the only published route to act runs 40 hours a week. Importance is 9 rather than 10 because the amount at risk on a Summit ticket is $155 adult (c15), real but not ruinous. Satisfaction is 3 rather than 1 because the phone line is toll free, staffed by people, and works well inside its window. Sizing caveat that belongs in the score, the direct share of bookings is UNKNOWN, no channel split is published, so the population this serves is bounded by a number nobody has published.

opportunities.job: When five ships are in port and I am needed on the platform, I want the routine questions already answered so I can load the train instead of repeating the fare table.
opportunities.current_workaround: One person switches between the ticketing system, three inbound channels and the platform, and the channel that waits is whichever one is not currently ringing.
opportunities.notes: The internal twin of the job above, and the reason the guest-side gap is not merely a courtesy problem. Their own job description puts the contact centre and the loading crew in the same body. Satisfaction is low because the collision is structural, not a staffing accident. No headcount split between year-round and seasonal is published, so the size of the affected team can't be stated.

opportunities.job: Before I commit $155 to $289 for my family, I want a fast, correct answer to my question, in my language, so I can book with confidence.
opportunities.current_workaround: Read the website, phone during the weekday window, email and wait, or ask the cruise line's shore excursion desk and buy there instead.
opportunities.notes: Satisfaction is 4 rather than lower because their site does publish fares, seasons and policies in detail, so a determined reader can self-serve today. The unserved slice is speed, out-of-hours, and language. Honest counterweight that must ride with this one, an experimental study of 467 German adults found booking intention significantly lower for chatbots than for humans and significantly lower in negative situations, with the two main effects significant and the interaction ANOVA insignificant (c45). This job is about answering, not about taking the booking, which is the distinction that keeps it viable.

opportunities.job: When the buy button fails, I want a way to still give this company my money, so the sale does not evaporate.
opportunities.current_workaround: Call 1-800-343-7373 or email info@wpyr.com, both of which route back to the same weekday window.
opportunities.notes: MANDATORY CAVEAT, an outage is a point-in-time observation and could be transient, and that caveat ships in the same breath every time. Satisfaction is set at 6 precisely because we have one day's sighting and no evidence of a standing condition. Importance is high because it is the money door. This is a monitoring and fallback problem, and AI is close to the wrong answer for all of it, which is why it does not become the target.

opportunities.job: When I need 180 people across three depots in two countries before the season opens, I want an applicant to reach a start date fast enough that they haven't taken another job.
opportunities.current_workaround: A jobs page, a recruiting profile on Coolworks, and an HR/Payroll Manager, with the coordination presumably by email and phone.
opportunities.notes: The evidence asymmetry is the whole story here. The industry precedent is the strongest MEASURED result in the file, and the local pain is INFERRED from the shape of the operation rather than cited. No time-to-hire, no applicant volume, no turnover, and no seasonal headcount split is published. They clearly do staff this railway every year. Also carries a live constraint, about 40 workers voted to join SMART-TD on April 8 (c33), so anything touching represented roles is a negotiation. Ranks fourth on Ulwick and would rank first on a pure evidence-of-outcome test, which is exactly the kind of tension the scoring exists to surface.

opportunities.job: When my train sells out, I want to have captured what that seat was actually worth.
opportunities.current_workaround: Flat published seasonal fares, and the cruise lines capture the spread on their own listings.
opportunities.notes: Biggest theoretical prize, worst data readiness. c14 is a per-ticket price difference on ONE product and must never be read as a revenue split, since no channel split is published. No passenger count, no load factors and no trains-per-day exist to model against. Pricing is also negotiated with cruise lines, one of which is a minority partner in the ownership group (c5), so it is a commercial relationship before it is an algorithm. Not a first build.

opportunities.job: When a guest bought through a shore excursion desk, I want to serve them as well as I serve my direct guests.
opportunities.current_workaround: The cruise line owns the guest record and the desk, and the railway sees them at the dock.
opportunities.notes: A purpose-built platform already exists for exactly this and sells itself as automation and integration rather than AI. The fact-checker called that the strongest and most honest finding in the package. The right advice here is a buy evaluation, not an Alaska AI build, and saying so is worth more than pretending otherwise.

opportunities.job: When I want to know what guests actually thought of the ride, I want it in my own hands rather than on someone else's platform.
opportunities.pain_source: Hard limit on this study, ZERO verbatim customer reviews were obtainable
opportunities.current_workaround: Unknown, and honestly stated as unknown. The blockage is on our side of the fetch, not evidence that they lack feedback.
opportunities.notes: Scored low on purpose. Satisfaction is a guess because we have no visibility, and an opportunity whose satisfaction score is a guess does not get to be the target. Belongs in the Later lane as first-party feedback capture.

opportunities.job: When a season date or an exception changes, I want every channel showing the same thing on the same day.
opportunities.current_workaround: Publish on the product pages and rely on partners to keep up.
opportunities.notes: Real, unglamorous, and mostly a content governance job rather than an AI one. The reseller half of the evidence was not re-verified, which is itself a reason to keep this out of the target slot.

opportunities.job: When a locomotive is due, I want to know before it strands a train.
opportunities.current_workaround: Unknown. No maintenance practice, system or pain is cited anywhere in the file.
opportunities.notes: Included so the map is honest about what it does NOT know. Predictive maintenance is a genuine rail category and there is not one line of evidence here to build on, no telemetry, no failure history, no cited complaint. Proposing it would be inventing a need.

target_opportunity.job: Resolve a guest's booking change, cancellation or pre-trip question at the moment it arises, including the 128 hours a week the reservation office is shut, and without pulling an agent off the platform while a train is loading.
target_opportunity.why: It tops the Ulwick math at 15, importance 9 plus a 6 point gap, and it is the only high-scoring job in the file where every component is the company's own published policy rather than an inference. The hours are on two independent product pages (c10), the phone-only change path is on the cancellation page (c11), the 24 hour clock and the $10.00 per person penalty are on the same page (c12), and the collision between answering and loading is in their own job description (c30). Torres cross-check. SIZING, real but bounded by an unpublished number, since no channel split and no passenger count exist, so the honest framing is that the first job of any build is to measure the volume nobody has published. MARKET POSITION, strong, they own the product other Skagway operators appear to resell (c50, not re-verified) and the direct fare is materially below a cruise line's listed price on the same ride (c14), so every direct interaction they keep is worth more to them than one they hand to a desk. STRATEGY FIT, high, self-service is the ordinary state of the port, with competitors on RezdyPay, FareHarbor and Peek (c51, not re-verified), so this closes a gap rather than inventing a frontier. CARE VERSUS SATISFACTION, the widest gap in the file, a 24 hour refund clock against a 40 hour service week. It also beats the hiring opportunity on the one axis that matters for a first build, its pain is cited rather than inferred, even though hiring carries the better outside evidence.
target_opportunity.forces: PUSH, strong. The guest's money is on a clock that runs through nights and weekends while the only published route to act does not (c10, c11, c12). Staff push is equally strong, the person who would answer the call is on the platform doing crossing-guard duty (c30) on a day when five ships were listed in port (c20). PULL, strong for the guest, an answer at 9pm Saturday in Spanish or Japanese beats a callback on Monday, and strong for the business, since a seat released before the 24 hour cutoff can be resold on a ride that usually sells out in advance (c14). ANXIETY, high and specific, and it is the force that decides the design. In Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149, the tribunal held Air Canada liable for a negligent misrepresentation by the chatbot on its own website and rejected the argument that the chatbot was a separate entity, noting it should be obvious that the company is responsible for all the information on its website (c44). The experimental study of 467 German adults found booking intention significantly lower for chatbots than for humans, and lower in negative situations, with the interaction effect insignificant (c45), so guests are measurably less willing to transact with a bot. HABIT, high. The 1-800 number is printed on the cancellation page and the product pages, a share of guests never touch the railway's own systems at all because they buy at a shore excursion desk (c13), and only 12 percent of tour, activity and attraction operators actively use AI (c42), so nobody in this market is normalising the new behaviour for them. VERDICT, push plus pull exceeds anxiety plus habit ONLY under a design that deliberately lowers both. Anxiety falls if nothing that moves money is decided by a model, if every answer cites the company's own published page, and if a human handoff is one click away. Habit falls if the new path is offered at the exact moment the old one fails, on the closed-office message and the outage message, rather than asking anyone to change what they do first. A design that ignores those two conditions loses this on the forces even though it wins on the score.

candidates.name: Guest contact triage and answer desk, AI on the language, rules on the money
candidates.our_build: RAG assistant over their own published material, fused with workflow automation
candidates.what_it_does: One intake layer across the website, the contact form and info@wpyr.com, in English, Spanish and Japanese (c31). It answers the repeat tail from a bounded corpus of their own published pages, fares (c15), seasons and exception dates (c16, c17), the cancellation policy and penalty (c12), boarding and channel information (c13), every answer carrying a citation to the page it came from and an honest I don't know that hands off. It NEVER changes, cancels, refunds or prices anything. A request that touches money is classified, structured into a work item with the guest's booking reference and the exact arrival timestamp, queued for the reservation office, and acknowledged to the guest with what happens next and by when. Out of hours, that timestamp is the whole point, it gives the office a record of when the request arrived relative to the 24 hour cutoff, which is a policy decision for them to make and a named prospect-side dependency. Eight weeks remain in the 2026 season (c16), so the first deployment is SHADOW MODE, drafting for agent review and logging the real question distribution, because after October 7 there are no more guest contacts to observe until late April 2027.
candidates.cost_of_delay: HIGH and calendar-driven. The season closes October 7, 2026 (c16) and the next one opens around late April 2027. Shadow mode inside the remaining eight weeks is the only chance until spring to observe the real question mix, the real out-of-hours arrival pattern and the real language mix. Miss it and the 2027 build is designed on assumptions for a second year running. Vendor-side configuration in this category runs one to four weeks (c48), so the calendar is tighter than it looks.

candidates.name: Self-service change and cancellation desk, deterministic, no AI on the path
candidates.what_it_does: A guest opens a link, authenticates against their booking reference, sees their departure, and changes or cancels it. Code applies the published rule exactly, a refund up to 24 hours prior minus the $10.00 per person penalty, and no refund inside 24 hours (c12). The seat returns to inventory immediately, which matters on a ride that usually sells out in advance (c14). Nothing here needs a model, and saying so plainly is the point. Every input is structured, every rule is fixed, and the whole thing can be tested exhaustively, which is precisely the case where Google's Rule of ML number one says do not be afraid to launch without machine learning.
candidates.cost_of_delay: MEDIUM. The value is realised across a whole season rather than in any one week, so a 2027 launch loses little against a late 2026 one. The dependency is what carries the delay risk, since the ticketing vendor's API access is a third-party conversation that takes as long as it takes and should start in the off-season rather than in April.

candidates.name: Voice agent on the 1-800 reservation line
candidates.what_it_does: Answers 1-800-343-7373 out of hours and at peak, handles hours, fares, season and exception dates, boarding and directions, captures change and cancellation requests, and transfers to a person on demand. It is on the list because the phone is the published channel for the highest-stakes contact they have (c11), and it is on the list to be compared honestly rather than to be defended.

rice.confidence: 40 percent, the heaviest discount in the set

candidates.cost_of_delay: LOW, and the calendar argues actively against it. Eight weeks remain in the season, so a voice agent shipped now would go live at the busiest, thinnest-staffed moment of the year with no time to tune, and it could not be honestly validated before it met real callers. This is the candidate most likely to be reached for first and it ranks fourth of five, which is exactly why it was scored rather than assumed.

candidates.name: Buy the commodity, an off-the-shelf tourism chat widget
candidates.our_build: No build. A buy recommendation we would not be paid for.
candidates.what_it_does: Configure a purpose-built operator chat product on the website. This category is priced and real, with published monthly list pricing of $95 for 80 chats, $195 for 200 and $295 for 500, no fixed-term contract, and an in-house conversation design team configuring it in one to four weeks (c48). A named operator result exists, Black Cat Cruises, a two-location New Zealand marine wildlife operator running up to four daily departures, reports about 500 conversations a month, around 60 percent of questions answered, and 10 hours a month of staff time saved (c47). That is a VENDOR-PUBLISHED case study, not independent, and the 10 hours is the trustworthy figure while the modelled $3,750 a month is not banked revenue and must never be quoted as such. It is here because MIT's NANDA work found buying from specialised vendors succeeded about twice as often as internal builds, and a shop that never says buy is not being honest about the alternatives.
candidates.cost_of_delay: LOW to MEDIUM. Configuration takes one to four weeks (c48), so it is the only option that could be live before the October 7 close and gather a partial season of real question data. That timing argument is the strongest thing about it.

candidates.name: Reservation office copilot, internal only
candidates.our_build: Digital employee, scoped down to an assistant rather than an autonomous one
candidates.what_it_does: A tool the agents use, not one guests see. It drafts email and contact-form replies from the company's own published pages, translates into Spanish and Japanese with the agent approving before anything sends (c31), pulls the booking context together before a call, and keeps one governed source of policy text so the cancellation rule, the season exceptions and the fares say the same thing everywhere. Zero guest-facing liability under c44, zero exposure to the c45 acceptance problem, because a human sends every word.
candidates.cost_of_delay: LOW. Internal tooling can be built in the off-season and adopted in April with no seasonal urgency, and adoption by a small team is easier to secure when nobody is loading a train.

provisional_pick.name: Guest contact triage and answer desk, AI on the language, rules on the money
provisional_pick.why_over_others: It is not the highest raw RICE score in the set and it is still the right pick, which is what the method means by scores framing a debate rather than deciding it. THE OFF-THE-SHELF WIDGET scored highest at 4.20, entirely because its effort is half a person-month. Its impact is 0.5 and it never touches the money path, so it leaves the target job exactly as unserved as it is today. The correct use of it is not as a rival, it is as a component. We would tell them to buy the commodity answering layer if it fits, at $95 to $295 a month against published list pricing (c48), and spend real money only on the part nobody sells them, multilingual intake across email, form and web, structured change-request capture with an arrival timestamp against the 24 hour cutoff, and a clean handoff into the reservation office queue. Recommending a purchase we do not profit from is the cheapest credibility available and we should take it. THE DETERMINISTIC SELF-SERVICE DESK scored 2.57 and has the highest impact of anything on the list, and it is the honest endgame rather than the honest start. Its reach is capped by a number nobody has published, and its riskiest assumption, the integration surface of a hosted third-party ticketing system that returned an unavailable message on the day we looked (c19, transient and stated as such), can't be retired from outside the company. Sequencing solves both. The triage desk's ticket log produces the exact missing number, which is what makes the self-service desk's business case computable instead of assumed. Build the thing that measures before the thing that automates. THE VOICE AGENT scored 1.28 and it is the option a less careful shop would have led with. It faces a decided tribunal ruling that puts the company on the hook for what its automated agent says (c44), measured evidence that booking intention drops with chatbots (c45), a latency bar that production systems routinely miss, no published call volume to size it against, and an eight week runway that would put it live at the busiest moment of the year with no time to tune. THE INTERNAL COPILOT scored 1.73 and serves the twin job while doing nothing for the 128 hours the office is closed. TWO HONEST CONCESSIONS BELONG IN THE HANDOFF. First, the single most valuable slice of this opportunity, applying a 24 hour rule and a $10.00 penalty and releasing a seat, needs NO artificial intelligence, and the feasibility gate should hold us to that rather than let it drift back toward a model. AI earns its place on exactly one node here, understanding an unstructured multilingual message well enough to route it, which is the messy-input node AI is genuinely good at. Second, the hiring opportunity scored 11 and carries the best measured outcome in the whole file (c46, with the size caveat). It lost the target slot because its local pain is inferred rather than cited, no time-to-hire or turnover figure is published, and about 40 workers voted to join SMART-TD in April (c33), which makes anything touching workforce terms a negotiation before it is a deployment. It rides to the Later lane with that reasoning attached. THE TIMING ARGUMENT IS THE CLOSER. The season ends October 7, 2026 and reopens around late April 2027 (c16). Eight weeks remain in which real guest contacts still exist to be observed. Shadow mode now, build through the off-season, live before the 2027 opening.
